title: Is "the value of the last Content-Type header" correct?
body:
### What is the issue with the MIME Sniffing Standard?

https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#supplied-mime-type-detection-algorithm says

> 1. If one or more Content-Type headers are associated with the [resource](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#resource), execute the following steps:
>    1. Set supplied-type to the value of the last Content-Type header associated with the [resource](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#resource).

But, Fetch generally tries to treat multiple headers as coalesced into one header with commas. It has [extract a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) instead, which IIUC has some differences with regard to charset processing.

This is most observable because HTML uses MIME sniff for navigations, and so inherits the "last header" procedure, instead of the "extract a MIME type" procedure. Thus I think per the current spec, something like

```http
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Type: text/xml
```

is supposed to parse as `text/xml`, whereas

```http
Content-Type: text/html,text/xml
```

is... well, it's not really clear, because there's some implicit conversion between bytes and MIME type records happening in the spec, but one reasonable interpretation is that we try to parse that as a MIME type and get a failure, and thus fall back to sniffing, which could be observably different.
